      "observations": [
        "All11owned paths and hunks read, including9browser-test setup changes. The patch separates a shared startup promise from Boolean readiness, delays idle/global notification observers until that promise, and moves the per-wait gate before callback registration and the no-currentWindow branch. Tests resolve the gate, await it and wait a tick before accessing the idle service; this avoids measuring real two-minute timing. No new assertions or scenario test is added.",
        "UI caller adds catch and return for expected rejection. Cancellation before ready installs unload listener early and resolves a per-wait shortcut without settling the shared startup promise. However waitForActive then returns fulfilled when unloaded, so the UI caller continues after await; fulfillment is not proof all visibility checks passed. Reuse existing focused startup/completion-contract claim. Current fixed source contains later reland phase, not proof the August original survived continuously. Parent owns future backout3473; it is grouped context, not audited here.",
        "Full selected accepted callback/cleanup body inspected. Current observer callback iteration still uses Set.forEach, reset uses for...of, and every computes Boolean display readiness; these are distinct local choices, not new loop policy. Cleanup removes different event function identities for activate/resize/window-position listeners than registration; existing focused claim remains separate. Dense variable/comment groups and missing logical separators around unload/control blocks are readability suggestions, not fresh runtime defects. Startup comment mentions original _ready promise although _ready is now Boolean: explain shared startup promise and shortcut when maintaining this code. No related cleanup claims are inferred from Done states.",
        "Current selected browser-position task has explicit expected URL/count messages; they are nonempty. New setup has no assertions. Later axe watcher source is separate later evidence, not an accessibility result for this patch. Linux screen-position behavior remains explicit bypass, while other platforms require bounds; no fresh timers, notification display, Windows, browser, lint/build or accessibility test ran.",
        "Read complete retained current Bug0–21/footer and full Phab creation-to-final timeline, all10actual inline bodies including2old-diff bodies, no summary edits. Initial startup-delay landing and release/ESR adaptations precede this follow-up. Uplift report says automated coverage exists but Daily/Beta unverified and requests QA verify at least two minutes: request is not execution. Moving work to MailGlue startup idle tasks is a tentative unrelated design proposal, not implemented rule.",
        "Reviewer asks to move callbacks below gate and notices no-window early return bypasses readiness. Author agrees and final owned source places that branch after the gate. Proposed synchronous early bail requires extra promise-state tracking; do not mistake proposal for adopted check. Reviewer requests JSDoc and test awaiting startup promise; owned source adopts both. Review of an old test catch says a rejection caught there would not be unhandled; author explicitly withdraws leftover experiment. Offline test unhandled active-user-lock rejection is a historical report; no reproduced failure here.",
        "August follow-up lands d44a825, then Bug reports consistent Windows browser-position timeouts and backout754d37/reopen. November reviewer requests changes because backed out. December revised diffs receive Toby approval and e3e80a relands, with148 clarified. PTO reviewer removal and final accepted state do not retroactively validate August patch or prove timer/cancellation fixes. Future backout3473 is a phase link only; no future-row audit credit. Try URLs, remote job logs and removed/added child revisions remain bounded external locators."

      "observations": [
        "Read all three changed paths and the full 157-line diff, including the complete new 101-line test. The first task sends deliberately misspelled content without enabling the before-send preference itself. The second explicitly enables that preference, opens the spelling dialog, waits until Close is hidden, clicks Send and waits for compose closure. Both assert the fake SMTP last message contains the generated Subject. They do not assert corrected body text, a cancellation result, dictionary choice or every send trigger.",
        "The production callback initializes dictionary UI and calls NextWord before hiding Close and showing Send for before-send mode. The final test uses waitForMutationCondition on Close.hidden rather than a fixed delay or merely looking for an existing Send element. The exact options contain the misspelled key attriubuteFilter in both initial and current test source; do not describe it as a checked hidden-only attribute filter. The callback/source ordering supports the selected readiness state, not a claim about all dialog startup failures.",
        "The shared newComposeWindow helper makes identity optional and accepts body. It uses body || generated greeting, so an empty string also falls back; it does not preserve every supplied string. It resolves after window load, compose-editor-ready when needed, and focus, returning composeWindow and subject. The JSDoc still says object without stating Promise resolution. No signature or default semantics were changed outside this owned test helper.",
        "Initial preference handling uses direct setBoolPref(true), then false only after the successful task; cleanup also clears an unrelated send-warning preference. Accepted current tests use pushPrefEnv to restore those preferences and await asynchronous login removal. Keep the later harness cleanup separate from this initial patch. The original manifest places tags = oauth under the newly inserted spell-check section; current source scopes the tag to the OAuth test. No test-selection or cleanup run was performed.",
        "Three changed Assert calls have nonempty messages that state expected behavior. The title fail refers to finding misspelled content, but the written task ultimately sends the message; no delivery failure is asserted. Manual grouping separates setup, trigger, readiness, send and receipt checks. Existing copied header comments are not a global documentation pattern. No SMTP message, UI, spell checker, test, build or lint was run.",
        "Read complete primary Bug 1975724 description, comments 0–2, updates and end controls. It points to related Bug 1974125 comment 7, whose body was not opened. The sparse primary tracker establishes the test request and landing metadata, not the earlier regression request or its outcome.",
        "Read complete D255199 timeline and all six actual submitted inline bodies: 1401775, 1401857, 1401864, 1402382, 1432780 and 1432785. Five historical request bodies were retained from one historical view; their actual bodies were read, not inferred from Done labels. There are no summary edits.",
        "The first reviewer suggests finding a visible Send button. Another reviewer requests waiting for spell-check readiness, and the author explains that the element can exist before it is ready. The final actual suggestion replaces polling Close.hidden with an attribute mutation wait. Exact landed code adopts that wait, including the literal attriubuteFilter typo. The source callback establishes the selected Close-to-Send transition. Do not turn the initial visible-button suggestion or the typo into recommended API spelling.",
        "The helper documentation suggestion makes identity optional and documents body; exact source adopts those fields. The helper still uses || and still has a non-Promise return annotation. A later reviewer asks for a dedicated test file because browser_sendMessage.js tests send triggers; final source creates browser_sendMessage_spellCheck.js. This is a scoped separation of test purposes, not a required filename convention for all tests.",
        "Historical Try links, completed builds, change requests and approvals remain distinct reports. No linked Try job or related bug was opened. No SMTP, compose, dialog, dictionary, cancellation, test, build, lint or accessibility run was performed."
